title: Rohit Sharma's Lord's Century Reshuffles ICC ODI Rankings Battle
excerpt: The veteran opener's record-breaking 138 at Lord's narrows the gap with Virat Kohli in the ICC batting rankings, while Shubman Gill continues to chase New Zealand's Daryl Mitchell for the No. 1 spot.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Rohit Sharma's 138 at Lord's boosts his ICC ODI ranking, closing in on Virat Kohli.
  • Shubman Gill scored 188 runs in the series, just 11 points behind No. 1 Daryl Mitchell.
  • India lost the ODI series 1-2 to England but retained the No. 1 team ranking with 116 points.
  • The rankings are crucial as the 2027 ODI World Cup approaches in less than a year.

The ICC ODI batting rankings are witnessing a multi-front battle involving three Indian batters, with Rohit Sharma's commanding century at Lord's threatening to redraw the standings heading into the 2027 World Cup cycle.

Entering the recently concluded England series, New Zealand's Daryl Mitchell held the No. 1 spot with 814 rating points, followed by India captain Shubman Gill at 803, Virat Kohli at 757, and Rohit at 744, according to CricTracker. After three matches against England and a parallel NZ-West Indies series, those margins have been compressed dramatically.

Rohit's Lord's Masterclass

Rohit began the England tour quietly, managing just 11 and 26 in the first two ODIs at Edgbaston and Cardiff. Then came July 19 at Lord's.

"Rohit and Kohli, this will always be a problem for them because an ODI series is generally of three matches. There is a series, then there is nothing for two months."

— Aakash Chopra, former India opener

https://youtube.com/watch?v=BzfN3Oo0QHY

Chasing 388, the 39-year-old opener hammered 138 off 110 balls in what Cricbuzz confirmed was the first ODI century by an Indian batter at the Home of Cricket. At 39 years and 80 days, he also became the oldest player to score an ODI hundred at the venue, surpassing Rahul Dravid's previous age record for India across all formats at Lord's.

> **"England remain seventh at 93 points.

For Rohit, 39, and Kohli, 37 — both now playing only ODIs at the international level — the scheduling challenge is acute. ODI series are typically three matches long with months-long gaps between them. India's next ODI assignment is not until September, creating an extended break that Chopra flagged as a structural disadvantage for veteran batters trying to maintain rhythm.

"England remain seventh at 93 points."You want to score runs."

The full post-series ICC rankings update will confirm the exact movement across all positions. For Indian fans, the key question is whether Gill can finally dislodge Mitchell from the top spot and whether Rohit's Lord's heroics have pulled him level with — or past — Kohli in the standings. With England's Ben Duckett (141 at Lord's) and Joe Root (249 unbeaten runs in the series) also likely to climb, the upper reaches of the ODI rankings table are set for their most competitive phase in years.
